w10_T4_005042: The flower festival opened the morning with 40 pots of lilies on the display bench. Before ten o'clock 11 pots were bought by early visitors. A grower arrived at noon with 72 fresh pots, which joined the bench. The marquee itself is 60 metres long. During the afternoon the stewards counted 3 stems standing in every pot, and each stem carried 6 open blooms. By evening the heat had wilted 991 of the blooms and they were snipped off. How many blooms were still on the bench at closing time?
w10_T4_005049: Marta collected 88 boxes of leaflets from the printer, and each box held 7 leaflets. The hall where the campaign meets holds 300 people. At the station 141 leaflets were handed out on the first morning. Her colleague Dan, whose own stack had run out days earlier, noticed that every remaining leaflet carried 7 discount vouchers along its edge. All those vouchers were then shared equally among the 5 shops taking part, and Marta delivered the bundle for the bakery. How many vouchers did the bakery receive?
w10_T4_005051: The athletics club took delivery of 150 crates of water for the meeting, and every crate contained 8 bottles. A dozen stewards were on duty at the gate, and the stadium seats 9000 people. The clubhouse fridge held 68 more bottles, and a steward found 3 loose bottles in the equipment store, so all of these were counted with the rest. Each bottle carries a deposit of 5 cents, and the club writes its deposits in cents rather than in dollars. What is the total deposit in cents on the club's bottles?
w10_T4_005052: The bike shop had 117 inner tubes on its wall rack when it opened in the morning, and the mechanics log every repair in minutes rather than in hours. Customers bought 37 tubes before lunch. The workshop used 9 more fitting them to hire bikes during the middle of the day. The shop has been trading for 23 years on the same corner. In the afternoon a wholesaler delivered 18 tubes, and in the evening 5 unopened tubes were returned by a cycling club. How many inner tubes were on the rack at closing time?
w10_T4_005059: A small publisher printed 217 copies of each of its 7 nature titles one autumn. A flooded lorry ruined 201 of the copies before they reached the warehouse. The print shop itself runs 24 hours a day. Every surviving copy contains 9 full-page photographs. A late supplement added 61 further photographs to the archive count. When the rights were reviewed, 3539 photographs had to be withdrawn from the collection. How many photographs did the publisher still hold the rights to?
w10_T4_005062: The village festival hired 217 trestle tables, and 4 folding chairs were set beside each table. Half of the chairs in the store are the old wooden kind. The primary school lent 77 extra chairs, and the church hall sent over 64 more. On the day 980 chairs were carried into the main marquee for the concert. A late van arrived with 34 additional chairs, which were stacked outside with the spares. How many chairs were outside the marquee?
w10_T4_005066: Marek had 65 bottle caps in his collecting tin. His friend Ines, whose tin was fuller than his, handed him 72 caps she no longer wanted. Marek then traded 75 caps away for a set of badges. The collectors club has 19 members. At the annual swap each cap he still owned was valued at 4 club points, and every club point could be exchanged for 8 raffle numbers. The organiser gave Marek 44 extra raffle numbers for helping to set up. How many raffle numbers did Marek hold?
w10_T4_005070: Anya started the month with 200 minutes of call credit on her phone, and her provider bills everything in minutes rather than in hours. Her brother Bilal, whose own credit was almost gone, transferred 29 minutes to her account. Anya then used 227 minutes over three long weeks of calls home. A loyalty offer added 30 minutes to her account at the end of the month. Half of her calls go to Bilal anyway. She used 19 more minutes on the last evening. How many minutes of credit did Anya have left?
w10_T4_005079: Tara kept 28 seed potatoes in a paper sack over the winter. In March she planted 23 of them in her allotment beds. From each potato still in the sack she later grew a plant that produced 5 new potatoes, and she gathered those in. Her family ate 22 of the harvested potatoes over the following fortnight. Her neighbour Femi, who had grown far more than she had, gave her one potato for every potato she had left, doubling her store. Tara then bought 61 potatoes at the market and put them in the same sack. How many potatoes were in Tara's sack?
w10_T4_005089: The scout troop had 131 cloth badges in its cupboard at the start of the year, and it records hike times in minutes rather than in hours. The district office sent 22 more badges in the spring, and a retiring leader donated 31 from her old kit. The troop then had every badge in the cupboard reissued in 3 colour versions, so the number tripled. It posted 130 badges to a partner troop overseas. How many badges were left in the cupboard?
w10_T4_005092: The Halden dairy milks 182 cows twice a day, and it records its output in litres rather than in hectolitres. Each cow fills 7 buckets over the course of a week. Customers at the farm gate bought 878 buckets straight from the cooling room last week. Hana bottles the milk while her brother Otto drives the van, and she found that every bucket left filled exactly 3 bottles. Each bottle then had 2 paper labels stuck on it, one for the neck and one for the body. How many labels did Hana use?
w10_T4_005107: The philatelic society kept 227 first-day covers in its display case. A member's estate added 42 covers in January, and a house clearance brought in 65 more. A dozen members attend the monthly meeting. At the spring auction the society sold 243 of its covers to collectors from out of town. Every cover still in the case carries 9 separate stamps. How many stamps are in the display case?
w10_T4_005112: The station car park held 25 cars when the barrier was raised in the morning, and it charges by the minute rather than by the hour. In the first hour 17 more cars drove in. Before nine o'clock 33 cars left for the early train connections, and 4 more drove out shortly afterwards. Over the afternoon 78 cars arrived for the shopping centre. In the early evening 26 cars left, and 55 arrived for the concert at the arena. How many cars were in the car park at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_005113: The little cinema had 110 tickets for the Saturday matinee, and it prints the running time in minutes rather than in hours. Half of the seats are up in the balcony. The morning box office sold 15 tickets. Just before noon a coach party bought 78 of them in one go. Over the early afternoon 13 more were sold at the desk, and 2 more went to walk-in customers. In the evening 1 final ticket was sold to a latecomer. How many tickets were still unsold?
w10_T4_005114: The village hall stored 129 folding chairs in its cellar, and the caretaker measures the rooms in centimetres rather than in metres. A closing church nearby donated 7 chairs, a school sent 53, and a wedding hire firm gave 61 that were surplus to its stock. The caretaker shared all the chairs equally among the 5 meeting rooms upstairs. He then worked only on the blue room, fitting 2 tie-on cushions to every chair standing there. How many cushions did the blue room need?
w10_T4_005115: The print room started the morning with a run of 104 large sheets. Before the break the manager doubled the run, so twice as many sheets were produced in total. Every sheet is perforated into 7 raffle tickets. During the afternoon 76 loose tickets were found in a drawer from last year's fair and added to the box. In the evening a committee member brought 77 tickets back from the reserve stock. How many raffle tickets were in the box?
w10_T4_005121: The smallholding kept 89 laying hens through the winter, and 8 more were bought at the spring market. Half of the flock are speckled brown. The farm lies 12 kilometres from the village. Over one week each hen in the flock laid 6 eggs. The ducks on the pond contributed 59 eggs, which went into the same trays. Every egg from those trays was sold at the roadside for 5 rupees. How many rupees did the smallholding take?
w10_T4_005122: The distribution warehouse counted 203 pallets on its floor first thing in the morning, and a forklift brought 3 more up from the yard. Every pallet on the floor is stacked with 8 sealed cartons. During the afternoon 49 loose cartons arrived by courier and were placed with the stock. In the evening 79 cartons came back from a cancelled supermarket order. How many cartons were in the warehouse at the end of the day?
w10_T4_005134: Ella started her charity fun run with 15 sponsorship cards already filled in, and her running time is recorded in seconds rather than in minutes. Her class handed her 44 more completed cards, her aunt's office sent 54, and the neighbours added 25. The course itself is 8 kilometres long. Every completed card is worth 5 fundraising points on the school board. On the final day the organisers announced that each point would count twice. How many fundraising points did Ella end up with?
w10_T4_005141: A tea factory had 230 wooden chests in its store, and a lorry delivered 23 more from the plantation. The building has 3 loading bays along its north wall. Every chest in the store is filled with 5 tin caddies, and each caddy holds 9 sealed packets of tea. The laboratory returned 32 sample packets that had passed testing, and they were added to the count. The factory weighs its tea in grams rather than in kilograms. How many packets of tea did the factory have?
w10_T4_005149: The swimming gala printed 150 programmes for the opening night, and the office found 24 more from the heats. Ticket demand meant the printer ran a second batch so that the pile became double its size. A club official then brought 20 programmes from the reception desk. For the regional tour the organisers ordered triple that pile, having 3 copies made of every programme. A cupboard search turned up 41 programmes from last season, which were added to the boxes, and race times are written in seconds rather than in minutes. How many programmes were in the boxes?
w10_T4_005150: The charity shop had 181 second-hand books on its shelves at the start of the week. Donations brought in 75 more books on the Tuesday. A dozen volunteers take turns behind the till. A clearance sale on the Saturday sold 255 books to a dealer who arrived with a van. The manager sent whatever was left to a printer, who produced 7 copies of it for the hospital reading group. Of those copies, 4 were given away at the first meeting. How many copies did the reading group still have?
w10_T4_005152: The market stall opened the morning with 73 wicker baskets on the trestle. Before eleven o'clock 26 baskets had been sold to café owners. The stallholder then found that every basket still on the trestle held 4 ripe pears. During the afternoon 142 pears were sold loose to passing shoppers. In the early evening the orchard van delivered 32 more pears to the stall, and a neighbouring grower handed over 38 pears he could not sell. How many pears were on the stall at the end of the day?
w10_T4_005159: Nadia had 235 glass beads set aside for her embroidery panel. Her friend Karim, whose own supply was much smaller than hers, gave her 70 beads from his workbox. She then bought 42 beads at the craft market on the corner. The pattern calls for 7 stitches to hold every single bead in place. Karim worked through one long weekend and completed 923 of those stitches himself. How many stitches were still to be sewn?
w10_T4_005166: The candle workshop opened the morning with 6 crates on the bench, and every crate held 36 candles. By midday 130 candles had been sold to the gift shop in town. During the afternoon the chandler poured and finished 19 new candles, which joined the others on the bench. In the evening every candle was boxed with 2 long matches for the winter market. The packer added 16 spare matches to the box of supplies. How many matches were used or set aside in total?
